item.text: South Australia’s Independent Commission Against Corruption examined corruption risks arising from lobbying public officials and the effectiveness of the state’s regulatory scheme.
item.support: This report examines corruption risks associated with lobbying and influencing activity aimed at public officials in South Australia

item.text: The Commission considered the scope of regulation, transparency, former officials’ lobbying, local government and administration of the scheme.
item.support: identified limitations in the scope of the scheme, the regulation of lobbied parties

item.text: The Commission concluded that the scheme exposed only a small proportion of influencing activity to public scrutiny.
item.support: In its present form the regulatory scheme in this state admits only a shaft of light on a small part of influencing activity.

item.text: Its 31 recommendations proposed broader coverage, disclosure of lobbying contacts, restrictions after public office, local government coverage and oversight by the Ombudsman.
item.support: That the scheme created by the Lobbyists Act and Lobbyists Regulations should be regulated and administered by the Ombudsman.

item.quote: Transparency is the best measure to combat the corruption risks associated with influencing activity.
